name: West Virginia

sales.rateNote: 6% consumers sales and service tax and use tax on goods and services. Municipalities that qualify may add a municipal sales and use tax of up to 1%; in a few economic opportunity development districts a special district excise tax replaces the state sales tax at the same 6% rate.

local.levies: qualifying municipalities (municipal sales and use tax, administered by the state Tax Division)
local.capNote: Municipal sales tax may not exceed 1% (W. Va. Code 8-13C-4).

groceries.note: The tax on food and food ingredients for human consumption ceased after June 30, 2013 (W. Va. Code 11-15-3a), after being cut to 3% in 2008 and 2% in 2012.

clothing.note: Clothing is taxable except during the summer sales tax holiday ($125 or less per item).

otherRates.item: factory-built homes used as a principal year-round residence
otherRates.note: 6% applied to half of the sale price; other factory-built home sales pay 6% on the full price.

holidays2026.name: West Virginia Sales Tax Holiday
holidays2026.items: clothing $125 or less; laptops and tablets $500 or less; school instructional material $20 or less; school supplies $50 or less; sports equipment $150 or less

sales.holidayNote: The holiday runs from the Friday before the first Sunday in August to the following Monday (four days).

useTax.note: 6% state use tax, plus municipal use tax where imposed, when sales tax was not paid.

facts.text: West Virginia's holiday lasts four days (Friday to Monday) and includes sports equipment up to $150, an unusual category.
Nonprescription medications are taxable; only drugs dispensed on prescription are exempt.
Groceries were taxed at 6% before 2008; the rate fell to 3%, then 2%, and the food tax ended on July 1, 2013.
Since April 7, 2025 (SB 615), businesses no longer make an accelerated sales tax payment each June.
Four developments (Charles Pointe, The Ridges, University Town Center, The Highlands) collect a 6% special district excise tax instead of state sales tax.

property.levied: county boards of education, county commissions, municipalities and the State

assessment.text: All property is assessed annually as of July 1 at 60% of its true and actual value (W. Va. Code 11-3-1). The state constitution divides property into four classes with different maximum levy rates.

homestead.name: Homestead Exemption
homestead.text: The first $20,000 of assessed value of a home occupied by its owner is exempt when the owner is 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled and a West Virginia resident (W. Va. Code 11-6B-3). There is no general exemption for other homeowners.
homestead.applyBy: Apply with the county assessor; the exemption attaches to the home occupied on the July 1 assessment date and applies to the following tax year.

otherRelief.name: Motor Vehicle Property Tax Adjustment Credit
otherRelief.text: Income tax credit for personal property taxes paid on time on eligible vehicles (cars, trucks, motorcycles, buses, trailers); leasing companies must pass it on.

dueDates.text: Payable in two installments: first half due September 1 of the tax year, second half due March 1 of the next year. A 2.5% discount applies to each half paid before its due date; delinquent taxes accrue 9% interest per year.

facts.text: Paying early earns a 2.5% discount on each half of the property tax bill.
Unlike most states, West Virginia itself levies a small share of property tax, alongside counties, school boards and cities.
Assessment is at 60% of market value: a home worth $200,000 is assessed at $120,000 before any exemption.
Vehicles are taxed as personal property, but owners can recover the tax through the Motor Vehicle Property Tax Adjustment Credit on their income tax return.
The homestead exemption for seniors and disabled owners is $20,000 of assessed value, which equals about $33,333 of market value at the 60% ratio.
